items.label: Squash
items.meal: Cut into wedges, toss with oil, salt and chilli flakes, and roast at 200°C for 35–40 minutes until the edges catch. Good with a spoon of yoghurt.
items.keep: Whole, somewhere cool and dry, it keeps for months. Once cut, wrap it and use within a week.
items.eat: No need to peel: the skin of most squash goes soft when roasted. Scoop out the seeds and roast them too for a crunchy snack.

items.label: Rainbow chard
items.meal: Slice the stems and fry them in butter with garlic for 5 minutes, then add the shredded leaves until they wilt. Pile onto toast or stir through pasta.
items.keep: Wrapped in a damp tea towel in the fridge, it stays perky for 4–5 days.
items.eat: Stems and leaves. The stems just need a few minutes' head start.

items.label: Tomatoes
items.meal: Chop, salt and leave for 10 minutes, then toss with olive oil and torn stale bread. That's a panzanella.
items.keep: Out of the fridge, stalk side down and out of the sun. The fridge dulls the flavour.
items.eat: All of it. Soft or split ones make the best sauce.

items.label: Leeks
items.meal: Slice thinly and cook slowly in butter with a pinch of salt for 15 minutes until silky. Fold through pasta, or pile on toast with cheese and grill.
items.keep: Unwashed in the fridge, they keep for 1–2 weeks.
items.eat: The white and pale green slice up best. The dark tops are tougher but good in stock or soup. Rinse grit from between the layers.

items.label: Lollo rosso
items.meal: Dress just before eating: 1 tsp mustard, 1 tbsp vinegar and 3 tbsp oil, shaken in a jar with salt.
items.keep: In a bag or damp tea towel in the salad drawer, 3–5 days. Limp leaves perk up in a bowl of cold water.
items.eat: Every leaf. The frilly red edges are just colour, not bitterness.

items.label: Cavolo nero
items.meal: Strip the leaves, shred them, and fry in olive oil with garlic and chilli for 5 minutes. Toss with pasta and lots of cheese.
items.keep: In a bag in the fridge, up to a week.
items.eat: Leaves cooked, or raw if you rub them with oil and lemon first. Chop the stems finely and fry them a few minutes before the leaves.

items.label: Fennel
items.meal: Slice as thinly as you can and toss with orange segments, olive oil and salt for a crisp salad. Or roast in wedges until soft and sweet.
items.keep: In the fridge, about a week.
items.eat: The bulb raw or cooked. The feathery fronds are a herb, like dill. The stalks are good in stock.

items.label: Green chillies
items.meal: Slice into scrambled eggs, dal, noodles or a fried rice. Heat varies, so taste a sliver first.
items.keep: In the fridge for up to 2 weeks, or freeze whole and grate straight from frozen.
items.eat: All but the stalk. Most of the heat is in the seeds and pale ribs, so scrape them out for a milder bite.

items.label: Radicchio
items.meal: Cut into wedges, brush with oil, and roast or griddle for 10 minutes. Finish with a drizzle of honey. Cooking tames the bitterness.
items.eat: The whole head. Tougher outer leaves are best cooked.

items.label: Peppers
items.meal: Roast whole at 220°C until blistered, cover in a bowl for 10 minutes, then peel and tear over toast with olive oil and salt.
items.keep: In the fridge, about a week.
items.eat: Everything except the stalk and seeds.

items.label: Pak choi
items.meal: Halve, fry cut side down in a hot pan for 2 minutes, then add a splash of soy sauce and water, cover and steam for 2 more. Serve with rice.
items.eat: Stems and leaves. The stems stay juicy and crunchy.

items.label: Spring onions
items.meal: Chop and stir through hot rice with soy sauce and sesame oil, or fold into an omelette.
items.keep: In the fridge, about a week. Stand the roots in a glass of water on the windowsill and they'll grow back.
items.eat: White and green. Only trim off the roots.

items.label: Fresh herbs
items.meal: Blitz a big handful of soft herbs with a garlic clove, lemon juice, olive oil and salt. Spoon this green sauce over eggs, potatoes or anything grilled.
items.keep: Stems in a glass of water, like flowers. Basil stays on the worktop; others go in the fridge, loosely covered.
items.eat: The soft stems of parsley and coriander chop up with the leaves. Woody stems like rosemary go in whole and come out after cooking.
